summary: Backend-only verification of the robust FP/TP close-reason classification. 4/4 pytest tests PASS. Tenant 'all' (real 5,299-row upload) reports false_positive_rate=14.4 (764/5299) and true_positive_rate=0.0 exactly as expected. Uploaded a 10-row mixed-variant XSOAR CSV to tenant 'acme-corp' with close reasons: False-Positive, Benign, FP (FP variants), True Positive, Malicious, Confirmed (TP variants), Other x2 + Duplicate x2 (neither). SOC Manager returned false_positive_rate=30.0 and true_positive_rate=30.0 (3/10 each), close_reason_mix retained Other=2 and Duplicate=2. Detection Engineering rule effectiveness reflected the same counting: RuleA fp_rate=100.0, RuleB fp_rate=0.0, RuleC fp_rate=0.0. After teardown, acme-corp rows=0 and tenant 'all' remained untouched at 5299 rows.
critical_code_review_comments: xsoar_ingest._is_tp() classifies 'mitigated', 'remediated', 'escalated' as TRUE POSITIVE. This may over-count TP in real data — 'mitigated' can just mean the incident was handled regardless of verdict. Consider narrowing to only explicit malicious/true-positive verdict tokens.

compute_detection_overlay uses `_is_tp(cr) or 'resolved' in (cr or '').lower()` for TP, but compute_soc_manager summary uses only `_is_tp`. This inconsistency means 'Resolved' close_reason counts as TP for per-rule precision/recall but NOT for the top-level true_positive_rate — verify this is intentional.

The MITRE tactic overlay is only enabled when the XSOAR CSV carries MITRE Tactic Name / Technique Name; without them the detection-engineering endpoint returns data_status=empty even when rule data exists (soft dependency worth documenting).
seed_data_creation: Temporary 10-row acme_mixed.csv uploaded to tenant 'acme-corp' via POST /api/upload/data?source=xsoar and deleted at the end via DELETE /api/dashboard/soc-manager/data?tenant_id=acme-corp. Tenant 'all' NEVER touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_fp_tp_classification.py is idempotent and safe to re-run — it always cleans up acme-corp. Uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from env; run with `-o addopts=""` if pytest.ini's xdist config causes issues. Tenant 'all' has 5299 rows (764 FP variants → 14.4%) and should be treated read-only.
rca of the issue: N/A — user's 14% FP-rate concern was a data-interpretation question, not a bug. The reported 14.4% is arithmetically correct (764 False Positive / 5299 closed). The change under test is a defensive enhancement to _is_fp/_is_tp to catch label variants (False-Positive, Benign, FP / True Positive, Malicious, Confirmed) so future uploads with different labelling conventions produce accurate rates. Verified both the sanity assertion on real data and the new variant-matching logic.
